subject: Pilot runway — ops risk-share credits vs. burst surcharge proposal
messages:
From: Eli Winters <eli@optilabs.ai>
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
Cc: Contracts Team <contracts@optilabs.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC economics — a couple questions before exec signoff

Sofia — thanks for the SOW and the usage estimates. A few items the finance and infra teams want to clarify before we route to procurement:

- We understand the 30-day timebox. Can you confirm what happens if we need two short bursts beyond the baseline (e.g., 6 hours each) during the evaluation? Will those be metered as overage at list rates or is there a credit bucket?
- Our security team asked whether there's an ops SLA credit if there is an outage affecting our KV-cache warmup (we rely heavily on prefix caching).
- Contracts want to see a one-page example invoice and a clear split of credits vs refundable deposit (if any).

Happy to hop on a quick call next week.

—Eli

Attachments: usage_estimates_optilabs.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
To: Eli Winters <eli@optilabs.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 13 Oct 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC economics — a couple questions before exec signoff

On Fri, Oct 10, 2026 at 09:12 AM Eli Winters <eli@optilabs.ai> wrote:
> Sofia — thanks for the SOW and the usage estimates. A few items the finance and infra teams want to clarify before we route to procurement:

Thanks Eli — quick answers inline and proposal below. Happy to review on a call Tuesday.

- Bursts: we offer two options for short bursts during the 30-day pilot:
  1) Credit bucket: we can seed a 500-credit burst bucket (non-refundable) that covers small, infrequent spikes. Unused credits do not roll forward.
  2) Metered surcharge: bursts billed at 1.5x baseline per-token rate (applies to sustained bursts beyond 4 hours).

- Ops SLA credit: for production SLA we provide credits. For pilots we can offer a capped ops risk-share credit up to 10% of pilot spend if a documented Redwood-side incident leads to >90th percentile latency degradation for >2 hours. This is a one-time goodwill credit applied as account credit.

- Invoice example: attaching a template and a clean SOW with a sample invoice line. We can also split the pilot purchase into a prepay credit (applied to usage) or a refundable deposit structure if procurement insists.

Proposal (pick one):
A) Burst-credit-first: Prepay $12k as pilot credit. Includes 100k tokens baseline + 500-credit burst bucket. Ops risk-share credit: up to 10% of pilot spend.
B) Metered-surcharge: Prepay $8k as baseline. Bursts billed at 1.5x and invoiced at month-end. Ops risk-share credit: up to 5% of pilot spend.

If OptiLabs wants a stronger commercial commitment, we can add a milestone-based rebate on conversion.

—Sofia

Attachments: poc_sow_v1.pdf (SOW), example_invoice.pdf
From: Asha Patel <asha@optilabs.ai>
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Contracts Team <contracts@optilabs.ai>, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Oct 2026 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC economics — a couple questions before exec signoff

Sofia / Marissa — thanks, this helps. A few follow-ups from procurement/legal:

- The refundable deposit option is their preferred path, but they need the term 'refundable' to be defined (timelines, burn conditions). Suggest splitting: $10k refundable deposit (returned minus actual usage) + $5k non-refundable burst seed.
- On the ops credit: procurement wants the credit to be automatic (not goodwill) and triggered by an explicit runbook/incident ticket. Can Redwood accept an objective trigger (e.g., >20% median latency uplift across three 15-minute windows) and automatic credit issuance to the HubSpot billing record?
- Also flagged: they want a rate cap if we convert to committed for 12 months. Is there a conversion discount ladder you can share?

Let us know if you prefer to mark up the SOW and iterate or have a brief legal-to-legal exchange.

—Asha

Attachments: redline_contract.docx (redline)
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Asha Patel <asha@optilabs.ai>, sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 10:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC economics — a couple questions before exec signoff

Hi Asha — looping in Ben for legal/pricing mechanics. Quick read: we can do the refundable deposit + burst-seed split with precise refund rules. Proposed language below you can drop into your redline:

- Refund mechanics: refundable deposit refunded within 30 days of pilot close (T+30) after reconciliation of actual usage. Any usage beyond the deposit is invoiced net 30.
- Burst seed: non-refundable, expires at pilot end.
- Ops credit trigger: agreed to objective metric. We will instrument automatic credit issuance when the following are met: (i) incident ticket created in Redwood incident tracker, (ii) three 15-minute windows where median latency uplift >20% relative to baseline, and (iii) postmortem signed by Redwood SRE. Credit applied as a billing credit within 14 days of postmortem acceptance.

Ben, on the conversion ladder: can we offer a 10% discount on per-token list rate for a 12-month conversion with a minimum commit of $120k ARR, 15% for $200k ARR? Also recommend a small conversion onboarding credit ($5k) if they convert within 60 days of pilot close.

—Marissa

Quoted text:
> On Tue, Oct 14, 2026 at 09:34 AM Asha Patel <asha@optilabs.ai> wrote:
> > The refundable deposit option is their preferred path...
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Asha Patel <asha@optilabs.ai>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC economics — ops risk-share credit wording + conversion ladder

Asha — thanks for the detailed redline. We incorporated the refund mechanics and ops-credit trigger as requested and added a short conversion ladder in Appendix B of the SOW. Key points you accepted on legal side:

- Refund: T+30 reconciliation, simple netting against usage, no surprise clawbacks.
- Burst handling: $5k non-refundable burst seed; additional bursts billed at 1.5x after 4 hours sustained.
- Ops credit: automatic issuance per the objective trigger; credit capped at 10% of pilot invoice and applied to the HubSpot billing record we referenced.
- Conversion discounts: 10% at $120k ARR, 15% at $200k ARR; $5k onboarding credit if conversion executed within 60 days.

If this matches OptiLabs' appetite we'll prepare the final SOW and a DocuSign link for the refundable deposit path (refundable deposit + burst seed). Planned next steps:
1) Final SOW + DocuSign (Redwood)
2) OptiLabs signs + pays refundable deposit via card/wire
3) Kickoff + instrumentation checklist (include KV-cache warmup trace)

If you want to switch to the meteredsurcharge approach before we sign, flag that now. Otherwise we'll deliver the DocuSign by EOD Friday.

—Ben
